feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the line and curve intersect twice, so we expect two solutions.

To find the coordinates of the intersection points, we take the equation of the line, replace $x$ and $y$ with the parametric formulas, and then solve for $t.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}x-1 \\ \frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-4 & =\frac{1}{2}(t+6)-1 \\ {t}^{2}-8 & =(t+6)-2 \\ {t}^{2}-8 & =t+4 \\ {t}^{2}-t-12 & =0 \\ (t+3)(t-4) & =0 \\ t & =-3,\,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the values of $t$ where the curve $x=t+6,\,y=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-4$ intersects the line $y=\frac{1}{2}x-1$ are $t=-3$ and $t=4.$
